method: visual PDF review plus curated sentence-level bilingual manuscript; cloze restored deterministically from the answer key printed in the source PDF and cross-checked against independent answer keys

articles.title: 完形填空 · 为什么求助并不意味着无能
articles.context: 文章解释人们为何常常不愿求助：暴露弱点、担心失去控制或被拒绝都会形成心理阻力；但研究显示，求助者往往比自己想象中更容易得到帮助，而且寻求建议反而可能让人显得更有能力。
rows: There are many understandable reasons why you might find it difficult to ask for help when you need it.
你在需要帮助时可能会觉得难以开口求助，这背后有许多可以理解的原因。
advance
Psychologists have been interested in this question for decades, not least because people's widespread reluctance to ask for help has led to some high-profile failures.
心理学家几十年来一直关注这个问题，尤其因为人们普遍不愿求助，曾导致一些引人注目的失败。
explain
Asking for help takes courage.
寻求帮助需要勇气。
emphasize
It involves communicating a need on your part—there's something you can't do.
这意味着你要表达自己有某种需要——有些事情你无法独自完成。
explain
In other words, you're broadcasting your own weaknesses, which can be uncomfortable.
换句话说，你是在把自己的弱点展示出来，而这可能让人不舒服。
explain
You might worry about coming across as incompetent.
你可能担心自己显得无能。
warning
You might have concerns about losing control of whatever it is you're asking for help with.
你还可能担心，一旦求助，自己会失去对那件事情的控制。
warning
Once someone starts to help, perhaps they'll take over, or get credit for your earlier efforts.
一旦别人开始帮忙，也许他们会接手一切，或者把你此前付出的努力归到自己名下。
example
Yet another factor that you might be worried about is being a nuisance or inconveniencing the person you go to for help.
你可能担心的另一个因素，是自己会成为麻烦，或给你求助的那个人造成不便。
advance
If you struggle with low self-esteem, you might find it especially difficult to reach out for help because you have the added worry of the other person declining your request.
如果你本来自尊较低，主动求助可能尤其困难，因为你还会额外担心对方拒绝你的请求。
explain
You might see such refusals as implying something negative about the status of your relationship with them.
你可能会把这种拒绝理解为：你们之间的关系出了某种负面问题。
warning
To overcome these difficulties, try to remind yourself that everyone needs help sometimes.
要克服这些困难，可以提醒自己：每个人都有需要帮助的时候。
encourage
Nobody knows everything and can do everything all by themselves.
没有人什么都知道，也没有人能完全靠自己做好所有事情。
emphasize
And while you might fear coming across as incompetent, there's actually research that shows that advice-seekers are perceived as more competent, not less.
而且，虽然你可能害怕自己显得无能，但研究实际上表明，向别人寻求建议的人反而会被认为更有能力，而不是更差。
contrast

Perhaps most encouraging of all is a paper from 2022 by researchers at Stanford University that involved a mix of contrived help-seeking interactions and asking people to recall times they'd sought help in the past.
也许最令人鼓舞的是，斯坦福大学研究人员2022年的一篇论文同时考察了人为设计的求助互动，并让人们回忆自己过去寻求帮助的经历。
report

The findings showed that help-seekers generally underestimate how willing other people will be to help and how good it'll make the help-giver feel (for most people, having the chance to help someone is highly rewarding).
研究发现，求助者通常会低估别人愿意帮忙的程度，也会低估帮助别人给施助者带来的良好感受（对大多数人而言，有机会帮助别人是非常令人满足的）。
report
So, bear all this in mind the next time you need to ask for help.
所以，下次需要求助时，把这些都记在心里。
conclude
Also, take care over who you ask and when you ask them.
同时，也要注意向谁求助，以及何时开口。
encourage
And if someone can't help right now, avoid taking it personally.
如果有人眼下无法帮助你，也不要把这件事理解成针对你个人。
encourage
They might just be too busy, or they might not feel confident about their ability to help.
他们可能只是太忙，或者对自己能否帮上忙没有信心。
qualify

articles.title: 阅读 Text 1 · 数字支付正在把小费推向更多场景
articles.context: 文章分析美国“小费扩张”和“小费通胀”：数字支付让商家更容易在服务前索要更高小费，虽然这能补充低薪服务人员收入，却也让小费越来越带有强迫意味，并与服务质量脱节。
rows: U.S. customers historically tipped people they assumed were earning most of their income via tips, such as restaurant servers earning less than the minimum wage.
历史上，美国顾客通常给那些被认为主要靠小费维持收入的人付小费，比如工资低于最低工资标准的餐厅服务员。
advance
In the early 2010s, a wide range of businesses started processing purchases with iPads and other digital payment systems.
2010年代初，各类商家开始使用 iPad 和其他数字支付系统处理消费付款。
sequence
These systems often prompted customers to tip for services that were not previously tipped.
这些系统常常提示顾客为过去并不需要给小费的服务支付小费。
conclude
Today's tip requests are often not connected to the salary and service norms that used to determine when and how people tip.
如今的小费请求往往已经与过去决定人们何时、如何给小费的薪酬和服务规范脱离。
advance
Customers in the past nearly always paid tips after receiving a service, such as at the conclusion of a restaurant meal, after getting a haircut or once a pizza was delivered.
过去，顾客几乎总是在服务完成后才付小费，例如用完餐、剪完头发或披萨送到之后。
example
That timing could reward high-quality service and give workers an incentive to provide it.
这种支付时点可以奖励优质服务，也能激励工作人员提供更好的服务。
explain
It's becoming more common for tips to be requested beforehand.
如今，服务开始之前就要求付小费的情况越来越常见。
advance
And new tipping technology may even automatically add tips.
新的小费支付技术甚至可能自动把小费加到账单里。
advance
The prevalence of digital payment devices has made it easier to ask customers for a tip.
数字支付设备的普及，让商家更容易向顾客索要小费。
explain
That helps explain why tip requests are creeping into new kinds of services.
这在一定程度上解释了为什么小费请求正逐渐进入新的服务领域。
explain
Customers now routinely see menus of suggested default options—often well above 20% of what they owe.
顾客如今经常会看到一列默认建议小费选项，其中往往有远高于应付金额20%的比例。
statistic
The amounts have risen from 10% or less in the 1950s to 15% around the year 2000 to 20% or higher today.
小费比例从20世纪50年代的10%或更低，上升到2000年前后的15%，再到如今的20%甚至更高。
statistic
This increase is sometimes called tipflation—the expectation of ever-higher tip amounts.
这种增长有时被称为“小费通胀”，即人们被期待支付越来越高的小费。
explain
Tipping has always been a vital source of income for workers in historically tipped services, like restaurants, where the tipped minimum wage can be as low as US$2.13 an hour.
对餐厅等历来依赖小费的服务行业员工而言，小费一直是重要收入来源；这类岗位的法定小费最低工资可能低至每小时2.13美元。
statistic
Tip creep and tipflation are now further supplementing the income of many low-wage service workers.
如今，小费适用范围扩大和“小费通胀”又进一步补充了许多低薪服务人员的收入。
explain
Notably, tipping primarily benefits some of these workers, such as waiters, but not others, such as cooks and dishwashers.
值得注意的是，小费主要让其中一部分员工受益，例如服务员，却未必惠及厨师和洗碗工等其他员工。
contrast
To ensure that all employees were paid fair wages, some restaurants banned tipping and increased prices, but this movement toward no-tipping services has largely fizzled out.
为了确保所有员工获得公平工资，一些餐厅曾取消小费并提高价格，但这种转向无小费服务的运动如今基本已经偃旗息鼓。
contrast
So, to increase employee wages without raising prices, more employers are succumbing to the temptations of tip creep and tipflation.
因此，为了在不涨价的情况下提高员工工资，越来越多雇主正屈从于扩大小费范围和提高小费比例的诱惑。
conclude
However, many customers are frustrated because they feel they are being asked for too high of a tip, too often.
然而，许多顾客感到不满，因为他们觉得自己被过于频繁地要求支付过高的小费。
contrast
And, as our research emphasizes, tipping now seems to be more coercive, less generous and often completely dissociated from service quality.
正如我们的研究所强调的，如今的小费似乎更具强迫性、更少体现慷慨，而且常常与服务质量完全脱节。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Text 2 · 英国医疗改革应从“修医院”转向提升全民健康
articles.context: 文章认为英国 NHS 面对新的健康挑战已经显得过时；真正的改革不仅要加强基层和社会照护，还要关注生活、工作和社交环境等健康决定因素，并把更多权力与资源交给更了解地方需求的领导者。
rows: When it was established, the National Health Service (NHS) was visionary: offering high-quality, timely care to meet the dominant needs of the population it served.
英国国家医疗服务体系（NHS）创立时具有前瞻性：它提供高质量、及时的医疗服务，以满足所服务人群当时最主要的需求。
advance
Nearly 75 years on, with the UK facing very different health challenges, it is clear that model is out of date.
近75年过去，英国面对的健康挑战已大不相同，很明显，这一模式已经过时。
contrast
From life expectancy to cancer and infant mortality rates, we are lagging behind many of our peers.
从预期寿命到癌症和婴儿死亡率，英国在许多指标上都落后于同类国家。
compare

With more than 6.8 million on waitlists, healthcare is becoming increasingly inaccessible for those who cannot opt to pay for private treatment; and the cost of providing healthcare is increasingly squeezing out investment in other public services.
超过680万人处在候诊名单上，对无力选择私人医疗的人来说，医疗服务正变得越来越难以获得；与此同时，医疗支出也越来越多地挤占其他公共服务的投资。
statistic
As demand for healthcare continues to grow, pressures on the workforce—which is already near breaking point—will only become more acute.
随着医疗需求持续增长，本已接近承受极限的医疗人员将面临更加严峻的压力。
warning
Many of the answers to the crisis in health and care are well rehearsed.
应对医疗与照护危机的许多办法，人们其实已经反复讨论过。
advance
We need to be much better at reducing and diverting demand on health services, rather than simply managing it.
我们必须更有效地减少并分流对医疗服务的需求，而不是仅仅管理已有需求。
contrast
Much more needs to be invested in communities and primary care to reduce our reliance on hospitals.
需要向社区和基层医疗投入更多资源，以减少对医院的依赖。
emphasize
And capacity in social care needs to be greater, to support the growing number of people living with long-term conditions.
社会照护能力也必须扩大，以支持越来越多患有长期疾病的人。
advance
Yet despite two decades of strategies and a number of major health reforms, we have failed to make meaningful progress on any of these aims.
然而，尽管过去二十年推出了多项战略和重大医疗改革，这些目标没有一个取得实质性进展。
contrast
That is why the Reform think tank is launching a new programme of work entitled “Reimagining health”, supported by ten former health ministers.
正因如此，Reform 智库在十名前卫生大臣支持下启动了一项名为“重新构想健康”的新计划。
report
Together, we are calling for a much more open and honest conversation about the future of health in the UK, and an “urgent rethink” of the hospital-centric model we retain.
我们共同呼吁，就英国健康体系的未来展开更加开放、坦诚的讨论，并“紧急重新审视”目前仍在沿用的以医院为中心的模式。
emphasize
This must begin with the question of how we maximise the health of the nation, rather than “fix” the NHS.
第一步必须是思考如何让国民整体健康达到最大化，而不是只想着“修好”NHS。
contrast
It is estimated, for example, that healthcare accounts for only about 20% of health outcomes.
例如，据估计，医疗服务本身只解释约20%的健康结果。
statistic
Much more important are the places we live, work and socialise—yet there is no clear cross-government strategy for improving these social determinants of health.
更重要的是我们生活、工作和社交的环境——然而目前并没有清晰的跨政府战略来改善这些健康的社会决定因素。
contrast
Worse, when policies like the national obesity strategy are scrapped, taxpayers are left with the heavy price tag of treating the illnesses, like diabetes, that result.
更糟的是，当全国肥胖治理战略之类的政策被取消后，由此产生的糖尿病等疾病最终需要由纳税人承担高昂治疗费用。
warning
Reform wants to ask how power and resources should be distributed in our health system.
Reform 希望追问：医疗体系中的权力和资源究竟应当如何分配。
ask

What health functions should remain at the centre, and what should be given to local leaders, often responsible for services that create health, and with a much better understanding of the needs of their populations?
哪些医疗职能应该保留在中央层面，哪些应该交给地方领导者？后者往往负责真正塑造健康的公共服务，也更了解当地居民的需求。
ask

articles.title: 阅读 Text 3 · 印度高温行动计划需要更本地化、更长期
articles.context: 文章讨论印度高温行动计划的不足：预警阈值常未因地制宜，资金和执行也不均衡；研究者主张结合湿度、夜间温度和社区脆弱性，并把植树、住宅改造等中长期降温措施纳入计划。
rows: Heat action plans, or HAPs, have been proliferating in India in the past few years.
过去几年，高温行动计划（HAPs）在印度各地迅速增加。
advance
In general, an HAP spells out when and how officials should issue heat warnings and alert hospitals and other institutions.
一般来说，HAP 会明确规定政府人员应在何时、以何种方式发布高温警报，并通知医院和其他机构。
explain

Nagpur's plan, for instance, calls for hospitals to set aside “cold wards” in the summer for treating heatstroke patients, and advises builders to give construction laborers a break from work on very hot days.
例如，那格浦尔的计划要求医院在夏季设置“冷病房”救治中暑患者，并建议建筑商在酷热天气让建筑工人暂停工作。
example
But implementation of existing HAPs has been uneven, according to a report from the Centre for Policy Research.
但据政策研究中心的一份报告，现有 HAP 的执行情况并不均衡。
contrast
Many lack adequate funding, it found.
报告发现，许多计划缺乏充足资金。
report
And their triggering thresholds often are not customized to the local climate.
而且，触发预警的阈值往往没有根据当地气候量身调整。
warning
In some areas, high daytime temperatures alone might serve as an adequate trigger for alerts.
在一些地区，仅凭白天气温偏高就足以触发预警。
qualify
But in other places, nighttime temperatures or humidity might be as important a gauge of risk as daytime highs.
但在另一些地方，夜间温度或湿度在衡量风险时可能与白天最高温同样重要。
contrast
Mumbai's April heatstroke deaths highlighted the need for more nuanced and localized warnings, researchers say.
研究人员表示，孟买4月发生的中暑死亡事件凸显了建立更细致、更本地化预警机制的必要性。
report
That day's high temperature of roughly 36℃ was 1℃ shy of the heat wave alert threshold for coastal cities set by national meteorological authorities.
当天最高气温约36℃，比国家气象部门为沿海城市设定的热浪预警阈值低1℃。
statistic
But the effects of the heat were amplified by humidity—an often neglected factor in heat alert systems—and the lack of shade at the late-morning outdoor ceremony.
但湿度——高温预警系统中经常被忽视的因素——以及上午较晚时段户外活动缺乏遮阴，都放大了高温的影响。
contrast
To help improve HAPs, urban planner Rajashree Kotharkar's team is working on a model plan that outlines best practices and could be adapted to local conditions.
为改进 HAP，城市规划师 Rajashree Kotharkar 的团队正在制定一套示范方案，概括最佳实践，并可根据当地情况调整。
advance
Among other things, she says, all cities should create a vulnerability map to help focus responses on the populations most at risk.
她表示，各城市至少都应绘制一张脆弱性地图，以便把应对措施集中到风险最高的人群。
emphasize
Such mapping doesn't need to be complex, Kotharkar says.
Kotharkar 说，这种绘图不必很复杂。
report
“A useful map can be created by looking at even a few key parameters.”
“哪怕只看几个关键参数，也能绘制出一张有用的地图。”
dialogue
For example, neighborhoods with a large elderly population or informal dwellings that cope poorly with heat could get special warnings or be bolstered with cooling centers.
例如，老年人口较多的社区，或那些简易住房较多、难以应对高温的地区，可以获得特别预警或增设降温中心。
example
The Nagpur project has already created a risk and vulnerability map, which enabled Kotharkar to tell officials which neighborhoods to focus on in the event of a heat wave this summer.
那格浦尔项目已经绘制了风险与脆弱性地图，因此 Kotharkar 能告诉官员，今年夏季一旦出现热浪，应重点关注哪些社区。
report
HAPs shouldn't just include short-term emergency responses, researchers say, but also recommend medium- to long-term measures that could make communities cooler.
研究人员认为，HAP 不应只包含短期应急措施，还应提出能够让社区更凉爽的中长期方案。
contrast
In Nagpur, for example, Kotharkar's team has been able to advise city officials about where to plant trees to provide shade.
例如在那格浦尔，Kotharkar 的团队已经能够建议市政府应在哪里植树以提供遮阴。
example
HAPs could also guide efforts to retrofit homes or modify building regulations.
HAP 还可以指导住宅改造或建筑法规调整。
advance
“Reducing deaths in an emergency is good target to have, but it’s the lowest target,” says climate researcher Chandni Singh.
气候研究人员 Chandni Singh 说：“在紧急情况下减少死亡当然是一个值得追求的目标，但那只是最低层次的目标。”
evaluation_quote

articles.title: 阅读 Text 4 · “欲望路径”揭示真实的人类空间选择
articles.context: 文章把城市中被人们自行踩出的“欲望路径”视为规划与行为互动的证据：它们有时被正式规划吸收，有时与控制性的城市设计发生冲突，也反映了人和动物共同寻找高效路线的倾向。
rows: Navigating beyond the organised pavements and parks of our urban spaces, desire paths are the unofficial footprints of a community, revealing the unspoken preferences, shared shortcuts and collective choices of humans.
在城市中规划好的道路和公园之外穿行时，我们会看到“欲望路径”——它们是一个社区的非正式足迹，显露出人们未明说的偏好、共享的捷径和集体选择。
advance

Often appearing as trodden dirt tracks through otherwise neat green spaces, these routes of collective disobedience cut corners, bisect lawns and cross hills, representing the natural capability of people (and animals) to go from point A to point B most effectively.
这些体现集体不服从的路线，常以被踩出的土路出现在原本整洁的绿地中：它们抄近路、穿过草坪、越过坡地，展现了人类（以及动物）以最高效率从A点到B点的自然能力。
explain
Urban planners interpret desire paths as more than just convenient shortcuts; they offer valuable insights into the dynamics between planning and behaviour.
城市规划者认为，欲望路径不仅仅是方便的捷径，它们还能让人看到规划与行为之间的动态关系。
explain

Ohio State University allowed its students to navigate the Oval, a lawn in the centre of campus, freely, then proceeded to pave the desire paths, creating a web of effective routes students had established.
俄亥俄州立大学曾允许学生自由穿行校园中央的草坪 Oval，之后再把学生走出的欲望路径铺成正式道路，形成一张高效的路线网络。
example
Yet, reluctance persists among other planners to integrate desire paths into formal plans, citing concerns about safety, environmental impact, or primarily, aesthetics.
然而，其他一些规划者仍不愿把欲望路径纳入正式规划，理由包括安全、环境影响，以及最主要的美观问题。
contrast

A Reddit webpage devoted to the phenomenon, boasting nearly 50,000 members, showcases images of local desire paths adorned with signs instructing pedestrians to adhere to designated walkways, underscoring the rebellious nature inherent in these human-made tracks.
一个专门讨论这一现象、拥有近5万名成员的 Reddit 页面展示了许多当地欲望路径：旁边竖着要求行人走指定步道的标牌，反而凸显了这些人造小径内在的反叛意味。
example
This clash highlights an ongoing struggle between the organic, user-driven evolution of public spaces and the desire for a visually curated and controlled urban environment.
这种冲突凸显了一场持续的拉扯：一边是由使用者自然推动的公共空间演化，另一边是对视觉上精心整理、受到控制的城市环境的追求。
emphasize
The Wickquasgeck Trail is an example of a historical desire path, created by Native Americans to cross the forests of Manhattan and move between settlements quickly.
Wickquasgeck Trail 是一条历史上的欲望路径，最初由美洲原住民开辟，用来穿越曼哈顿森林并快速往返各个聚居地。
story
This trail, when Dutch colonists arrived, was widened and made into one of the main trade roads across the island, known at the time as de Heere Straat, or Gentlemen's Street.
荷兰殖民者到来后，这条路被拓宽，成为横贯岛屿的主要贸易道路之一，当时称作 de Heere Straat，即“绅士街”。
sequence
Following the British assumption of control in New York, the street was renamed Broadway.
英国接管纽约后，这条街被改名为 Broadway。
sequence
Notably, Broadway stands out as one of the few areas in NYC that defies the grid-based system applied to the rest of the city, cutting a diagonal across parts of the city.
值得注意的是，Broadway 是纽约市少数不遵循全城网格系统的区域之一，它以斜线穿过城市的一部分。
emphasize
In online spaces, desire paths have sparked a fascination that can approach obsession, with the Reddit page serving as a hub.
在网络空间里，欲望路径激起的兴趣有时近乎痴迷，而这个 Reddit 页面就成了聚集地。
advance
Contributors offer a wide array of stories, from little-known new shortcuts to long-established alternate routes.
参与者分享各种故事，从鲜为人知的新捷径到存在已久的替代路线都有。
explain
Animal desire paths, such as ducks forging trails through frozen ponds or dogs carving direct routes in gardens, highlight the adaptability of these trails in both human and animal experiences.
动物也会走出欲望路径，例如鸭子在结冰的池塘上踩出路线，或狗在花园里开出直路；这些例子凸显了这类路径在人类和动物经验中的适应性。
example

As desire paths criss-cross through both physical and virtual landscapes, they stand as a proof of the collective insistence on forging unconventional routes and embracing the spirit of communal choice.
当欲望路径纵横于现实与虚拟空间，它们成为一种证明：群体始终坚持开辟非常规路线，并拥抱共同选择的精神。
conclude

articles.title: 阅读 Part B · 让工作中的新建议真正被认真对待
articles.context: 文章给出在职场推动新想法的五个步骤：主动推销方案、善用同事和利益相关者渠道、保持谦逊、尊重旧方案的历史价值，并用积极而现实的语言表达改进。
rows: Five Steps to Suggesting a Change at Work That'll Actually Get Taken Seriously
让工作中的改变建议真正得到认真对待的五个步骤
advance
Everyone wants to be that person—the one who looks at the same information as everyone else, but who sees a fresh, innovative solution.
每个人都希望成为这样的人：面对与别人相同的信息，却能看出一个新鲜而创新的解决方案。
advance
However, it takes more than simply having a good idea.
然而，仅仅有一个好点子还不够。
contrast
How you share it is as important as the suggestion itself.
你如何提出这个点子，与点子本身同样重要。
emphasize
Why?
为什么？
ask
Because writing a new script—literally or figuratively—means that other team members will have to adapt to something new.
因为，无论从字面还是比喻意义上，写出一套“新剧本”都意味着其他团队成员必须适应新东西。
explain
Not to mention, if the process you're scrapping is one someone else suggested, there's the possibility of hurt feelings.
更不用说，如果你准备废弃的流程正是别人提出的，对方还可能因此感到受伤。
warning
To gain buy-in on an innovative, new idea, follow these steps:
要让别人接受一个创新的新点子，可以按以下步骤来做：
advance
Be a salesman.
做一个推销者。
emphasize
Great ideas don't stand alone.
好点子不会自动站稳脚跟。
emphasize
In other words, you can't mention your suggestion once and expect it to be adopted.
换句话说，你不能只提一次建议，就期待它自动被采纳。
explain
To see a change, you'll need to champion your plan and sell its merits.
如果想看到改变，你需要积极为方案站台，并把它的优点推销出去。
encourage
In addition, you need to be willing to stand up to scrutiny and criticism and be prepared to explain your innovation in different ways for various audiences.
此外，你要愿意接受审视和批评，并准备好针对不同听众，用不同方式解释自己的创新。
encourage
Use channels.
利用渠道。
emphasize
Sometimes it makes sense to go to your boss first.
有时候，先去找老板是合理的。
qualify
But other times, it's useful to build a coalition among your co-workers or other stakeholders.
但在另一些时候，在同事或其他利益相关者中建立联盟会更有用。
contrast

When it works, it works great—because you're ready for your stubborn supervisor's pushback with answers like, “Actually, I connected with a few people in our tech department to discuss how much time these kinds of website updates would take, and they suggested they have the bandwidth.”
如果这种做法奏效，效果会很好——因为面对固执上司的反对，你已经可以回应：“其实，我联系了技术部门的几个人，讨论过这类网站更新需要多长时间，他们说目前有余力来做。”
dialogue
Be humble.
保持谦逊。
emphasize
One of the biggest barriers to gaining buy-in occurs when the owner of an idea is viewed as argumentative, defensive, or close-minded.
要让别人接受一个点子，最大的障碍之一，就是点子的提出者被视为好争辩、防御性强或思想封闭。
warning
Because, let's be honest: No one likes a know-it-all.
说实话，没有人喜欢自以为什么都懂的人。
emphasize
So, if people disagree with you, don't be indignant.
所以，如果别人不同意你，不要愤愤不平。
encourage
Instead, listen to their concerns fully, try to understand their perspective, and include their concerns (and possible remedies) in future discussions.
相反，要完整听取他们的担忧，努力理解他们的视角，并在之后的讨论中纳入这些担忧以及可能的补救办法。
encourage

So, instead of saying, “Martha, our current slogan is confusing and should be updated,” you could try, “Martha raises a great point that our current slogan has a long history for our stakeholders, but I wonder if we might be able to brainstorm a tagline that could build on that—and be clearer for new customers.”
因此，与其说“玛莎，我们现在的口号很混乱，应该更新”，不如试着说：“玛莎提出了一个很好的观点，我们现在的口号对利益相关者来说历史悠久；不过我在想，我们是否可以在此基础上一起构思一句对新顾客更清楚的宣传语。”
dialogue
Respect the past.
尊重过去。
emphasize
New ideas are the grandchildren of old ones.
新点子是旧点子的“孙辈”。
compare
In other words, don't throw old solutions under the bus to make your improvement stand out.
换句话说，不要为了突出自己的改进方案，就把旧方案贬得一无是处。
warning
Remember that in light of whatever the problem the old system solved—or, maybe, has failed to solve in recent memory—it was a great idea at the time.
要记住，无论旧系统解决了什么问题——或者它近来没能解决什么问题——在当时，它都曾是一个很好的主意。
qualify
Appreciating the older contributions as you suggest future innovations helps bolster the credibility of your idea.
在提出未来创新时肯定过去的贡献，有助于增强你这个点子的可信度。
explain
Stay positive.
保持积极。
emphasize
When pitching a new idea, it's important to use the language of abundance instead of the language of deficit.
推介新点子时，重要的是使用“充足”的语言，而不是“缺陷”的语言。
explain
Instead of saying what is wrong, broken, or suboptimal, talk about what is right, fixable, or ideal.
不要只说哪里错误、损坏或不够理想，而要谈什么是正确的、可以修复的、理想的。
contrast
For example, try, “I can see lots of applications for this new approach” rather than, “This innovation is the only way.”
例如，可以说“我能看到这种新方法有很多应用场景”，而不要说“这种创新是唯一的办法”。
example
Be optimistic but realistic, and you will stand out.
保持乐观，同时脚踏实地，你就会脱颖而出。
conclude

articles.title: 翻译 · 沉默在陌生人和朋友对话中的作用不同
articles.context: 研究表明，谈话中的长停顿并不总是负面的：陌生人之间的长停顿往往削弱联系感并促使换话题，而朋友之间的长停顿反而可能提供反思和表达的自然空间。
rows: You know the moment—the conversation slows, then there's a pause.
你一定熟悉这样的时刻——谈话慢了下来，随后出现一阵停顿。
story
It's awkward, and so awkward that some people will panic and say anything.
场面很尴尬，甚至尴尬到有些人会慌起来，随便说点什么来填补空白。
emphasize
Do we all find such silences so stressful?
我们都会觉得这样的沉默如此令人紧张吗？
ask

Researchers analysed the frequency and impact of gaps greater than 2 seconds during conversations, including an overview of previous studies which indicate that the fear of awkward silences can be so extreme that people avoid talking to strangers, even though doing so is likely to be an enjoyable experience.
研究人员分析了谈话中超过2秒停顿的出现频率及其影响，并梳理了以往研究；这些研究表明，人们对尴尬沉默的恐惧有时会强烈到让他们避免与陌生人交谈，尽管这种交谈很可能是一种愉快的体验。
report
During conversations with short gaps, people feel more connected to their conversation partners.
在只有短暂停顿的谈话中，人们会觉得自己与交谈对象联系得更紧密。
explain
But such feelings of connection markedly dip when entering a long gap.
但一旦出现较长停顿，这种联系感就会明显下降。
contrast
Long gaps between strangers are likely to be followed by a change in topic.
陌生人交谈时，较长的停顿之后往往会出现话题转换。
explain
But the opposite seems to be true for conversations between friends.
但朋友之间的谈话似乎恰恰相反。
contrast
Long gaps there saw increased connection.
在朋友之间，较长停顿反而伴随着更强的联系感。
contrast
Between friends, longer gaps seem to provide natural moments for reflection and expression.
朋友之间，较长的停顿似乎为思考与表达提供了自然而然的时刻。
conclude
